findings.title: Embedded post author link uses the wrong light-theme shade
findings.body: The original author-link color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this changes the light-theme branch to 70% while using 30% for the dark branch. This reverses the intended shades and alters the existing light theme rather than only adding the corresponding dark-theme color. Preserve the 30% primary value and use `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message length hint reverses the intended theme shades
findings.body: This hint previously used a 70% lightness adjustment of `$primary`, but the new light-theme branch is 30%, so the light-theme appearance regresses. It is also inconsistent with the desktop modal rule for the same hint. The dark-theme alternative should be the complementary `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)` while retaining `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` as the first argument.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading no longer preserves its original light-theme color
findings.body: The topic-map `h3` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`; this replacement changes it to 50% in the light branch. Thus the PR modifies light-theme contrast instead of solely providing the dark-theme equivalent, and it no longer matches the desktop topic-map heading. Use primary at 20% and secondary at 80%.

findings.title: Group member name loses its original emphasized color
findings.body: The `.group-member-info .name` color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the change uses 50% for both branches. This makes the name dimmer in light themes and removes its distinction from the title. Retain the 30% primary color and add the complementary 70% secondary color for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile group member name uses an incorrect lightness mapping
findings.body: This is the mobile counterpart of the group-member name styling and likewise changes the existing primary lightness from 30% to 50%. Consequently light-theme styling regresses and diverges from the intended emphasis. It should choose primary at 30% for light themes and secondary at 70% for dark themes.
